value_domain: Age group at AMEP registration
value_source: ACIL Allen Consulting, AMEP Evaluation, final report to the Department of Education and Training, 22 May 2015
variable_description: The client's age band on the day they registered with an AMEP provider, not their age at arrival, at visa grant or at any class. The gap matters because registration and tuition are separate steps: the AMEP evaluation records that "For clients 18 years and older, registration with the AMEP must occur within six months of arrival in Australia and classes must commence within 12 months." So a client can be a year older than this band by the time the first tuition hours appear in the AMEP quarterly columns. The band sits on the treated client profile row beside REGISTRATION_DATE, YEAR_OF_BIRTH and MONTH_OF_BIRTH, which together give exact age at any later event.
value_definition: A grouped age label rather than completed years, fixed once at the registration date. The band boundaries are the department's own reporting groups and the PLIDA item list does not publish them, so the width of the youngest and oldest groups is unknown.
limitation: It does not age with the file. A client placed in a young band when they registered in 2004 was well into middle age by the 2019 quarterly hours columns, so using this field as an age control across the tuition panel can misdate a person by more than a decade. It also cannot stand in for age at eligibility, since the program admits people aged 18 and over with a separate pathway for 15 to 17 year olds, and a band cannot separate those two groups.
rationale: The evaluation commissioned by the AMEP's own department sets out the registration step, its timing relative to arrival and the start of classes, and the adult eligibility rule, which is what distinguishes this field from an age at arrival or an age at first class.
evidence_quote: For clients 18 years and older, registration with the AMEP must occur within six months of arrival in Australia and classes must commence within 12 months.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed the custodian's wording, 'Client age group at time of registration with AMEP', with the domain guessed from the variable name as 'Age in completed years (inferred)', which is the wrong shape for a banded field, and with the inference warning printed as the limitation.

value_definition: A non-negative count of tuition hours in hours, for one client in this one period, drawn against the same 510 hour AMEP entitlement as classroom tuition rather than a separate allowance. limitation: A distance learning figure is not a marker of remoteness. rationale: The department's own evaluation names distance learning as one of the three tuition modes inside the 510 hour entitlement, and the Home Affairs distance learning page names the national provider and the circumstances that put a client into the mode, which is what separates this column from the classroom column beside it.

value_domain: Program-funded childcare hours used in 2011 Quarter 3
value_source: National ELT Accreditation Scheme, Standards and Criteria for AMEP Accreditation 2009, hosted by the Australian Council of TESOL Associations
variable_description: Hours of program-funded childcare used for an Adult Migrant English Program client's children in Quarter 3 of 2011. This is the first quarter of the childcare panel. The hours are recorded against the parent who is the client rather than against the child, and the column is one cell of the quarterly panel in amep_clientshours_2011_19 that runs to 2019 Quarter 2, so a family's series reads across a row. Childcare is a support service rather than tuition, and the accreditation manual for the program sets it as a standard in its own right: "Childcare provision is appropriate to the needs of clients."
value_definition: A count of care hours between 1 July 2011 and 30 September 2011, non-negative, sitting on the same client row as the tuition hour columns AMEP_2011_Q3, AMEPDL_2011_Q3, SPP_2011_Q3, SPPDL_2011_Q3, SLPT_2011_Q3 and HTS_2011_Q3; there is no EXTEND_2011_Q3, because that hour type starts only at 2017 Quarter 3. Childcare sits under support services in the 2009 accreditation standards rather than under program delivery, so these are service-use hours and not tuition hours; the sources do not say how, if at all, they bear on a client's tuition entitlement.
limitation: It does not say how many children were cared for or which ones: CHILDCARE_REQUIRED holds the count and CHILD_CHILDCARE_CENTRE the child-to-centre pairing, and neither is dated. An empty cell is also ambiguous, since a client with no children, a client who arranged care privately and a person who was not enrolled that quarter all leave the same blank. Care used before July 2011 is not in this table at all, so a client who studied from 2008 and needed care throughout shows nothing here for the first three years and looks like a new user of childcare.
rationale: The accreditation manual documents childcare as a funded support service of the program with its own accreditation standard, which is what makes this a service-use measure rather than a tuition measure.
evidence_quote: Childcare provision is appropriate to the needs of clients.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the custodian's label and used the generic no-value-list sentence for both the value definition and the limitation, so it never said whose hours these are, that they are not tuition, or what an empty cell means.

value_domain: ARMS client identifier
value_source: National ELT Accreditation Scheme, Standards and Criteria for AMEP Accreditation 2009, hosted by the Australian Council of TESOL Associations
variable_description: The client number the program's own case system gave this person, and the key that joins the six AMEP tables to each other. It therefore travels with registration, hours, English proficiency, CSWE awards and address for the same client, while SYNTHETIC_AEUID is the separate column that reaches the PLIDA spine.

It repeats for the same client across the hours, client profile, CSWE award, English proficiency and address tables, and appears in no other PLIDA dataset.

A client's Centrelink, tax, Census or health records are found through SYNTHETIC_AEUID, not through this number, so it cannot be used as a person key for the asset. It is also not the only ARMS client number on the AMEP tables: amep_englishproficiency carries a second one, CLNT_ID, which the custodian describes as the identifier used to report competency achievements, so the two columns should not be joined as though they were interchangeable without first checking that they agree.

evidence_quote: NEAS does not monitor outcomes; these are directly monitored by DIAC through statistical data made available via the AMEP Reporting and Management System (ARMS).

value_domain: Date the case system flagged the client as exited from the program
value_source: National ELT Accreditation Scheme, Standards and Criteria for AMEP Accreditation 2009, hosted by the Australian Council of TESOL Associations
variable_description: The day the program's case system, ARMS, recorded this client as having left the Adult Migrant English Program. The word flagged is doing work: the exit is a status a provider or the system set in the AMEP Reporting and Management System, not an event the client reported. It sits beside ENTITLEMENT_END_DATE on the same client profile row, and the two answer different questions, one being when the department closed the client and the other being when the tuition entitlement lapses whether or not the client ever attended.
value_definition: A calendar date with an open domain, bounded below by the earliest program registration in the collection and above by the extract day carried in DATE_EXTRACTED. One value per client, held on the client profile table rather than on an episode row.
limitation: It does not date the end of study. A client who simply stops coming is flagged when the provider or the system gets to it, so the gap between the last quarter with hours in amep_clientshours_2011_19 and this date can run to several quarters. A client still on the books at extraction carries no date rather than a future one, so treating a missing value as censoring and a present value as an event will mix administrative tidying in with genuine exits.
rationale: The accreditation manual establishes ARMS as the departmental reporting and management system whose records the department, not the provider's teaching staff, uses to monitor the program, which is what makes this an administrative flag rather than a reported event.
evidence_quote: NEAS does not monitor outcomes; these are directly monitored by DIAC through statistical data made available via the AMEP Reporting and Management System (ARMS).

value_domain: Reason type recorded when a client was flagged as exited
value_source: National ELT Accreditation Scheme, Standards and Criteria for AMEP Accreditation 2009, hosted by the Australian Council of TESOL Associations

It pairs with ARMS_FLAGGED_EXIT_DATE, and together they are the only record on the asset of how a person's participation ended. The categories come from the AMEP Reporting and Management System that the department uses to monitor the program, so they are administrative reasons chosen by a provider, and the registry publishes no code list for them.

It is also not the result of an exit assessment: the accreditation manual lists "results of student exit assessments" among the provider records that its panels do not normally examine, and those results never reach this table, so a proficiency outcome has to come from amep_englishproficiency instead.

rationale: The Home Affairs program page states the childcare offer and its age limit, which is what the count is a count of.

supersedes_rationale: The entry showed the custodian's wording, 'Number of children who require childcare service', with no value domain and the generic sentence duplicated in both the value definition and the limitation, so a reader could not tell a stated need from a delivered place.

value_domain: ARMS client identifier used for competency reporting
value_source: Department of Home Affairs, Evaluation of the Adult Migrant English Program New Business Model (Social Compass, 2019)
variable_description: The AMEP client number used to attach competency and assessment records to a person, carried on the English proficiency table beside AMET_CLNT_ID. The system that issues it is the AMEP Reporting and Management System (ARMS), the provider-facing database in which service providers record attendance, progress and assessment. It is an administrative key of the program, not a PLIDA key: SYNTHETIC_AEUID is the column that links a client to the rest of the asset.
value_definition: An opaque provider-system identifier issued by ARMS. It has no classification behind it and carries no information about the person; its only job is to tie the ACSF and ASLPR assessment columns on this table back to one client.
limitation: Do not assume it equals AMET_CLNT_ID, which sits on the same row. The item list distinguishes them precisely because the competency reporting stream used its own client number, so joining assessment records on the wrong one silently drops clients.
rationale: The evaluation names ARMS and describes it as the system in which providers record student progress and assessment against the ACSF, which is the reporting stream this identifier serves.
evidence_quote: Currently, providers continue to use ARMS, but must enter extra program data, including student attendance, student progress, child care attendance, and tuition streams into spreadsheets that must be submitted to the department.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's wording and gave the generic 'no finite value list' sentence twice, so it never explained what ARMS is, why a second client number exists on this table, or that it is not the linking key.

value_domain: Country of birth of the AMEP client
value_source: ABS, Standard Australian Classification of Countries (SACC), latest release
variable_description: The country the AMEP client was born in, as held on their client profile in the program's own records. The evaluation reports that AMEP students come from 197 countries and speak 267 languages, so the field is spread thinly across a very large number of categories. Country of birth in PLIDA is normally carried on the ABS Standard Australian Classification of Countries, which has 255 country categories grouped into 27 minor groups and nine major groups.
value_definition: A country code or country name. Where the ABS classification applies, the base level is a four-digit country code such as 5101 Myanmar, aggregating to a two-digit minor group and a one-digit major group by geographic proximity.
limitation: Whether the codes on this column are ABS four-digit country codes or the department's own country list is not stated in the item list, so the codes should be checked in the environment before they are mapped; a mismatch shows up as a large residual rather than as an error.
rationale: The ABS publishes the classification that country of birth is normally coded to in PLIDA and gives its structure and code form, which is what a reader needs before using the column; the classification actually applied to this Home Affairs column is not published.
evidence_quote: The country level is the base level of the classification. There are 255 country categories including four residual ('not elsewhere classified') categories.
supersedes_rationale: The entry inferred a SACC domain from the variable name and printed the generic sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so it asserted a classification without saying that the assertion was an inference to be checked.

value_domain: Year the CSWE course was accredited as a VET accredited course
value_source: Australian Skills Quality Authority, Course accreditation
variable_description: The year a Certificates in Spoken and Written English course was accredited as a national VET course, held on the award reference table, not against a client. The Australian Skills Quality Authority is the national VET regulator and says it "accredits courses where a clearly demonstrated training need cannot be met through a nationally endorsed training package qualification". The year therefore dates the version of the course, which is how two CSWE award codes with the same certificate name are told apart.
value_definition: A four-digit calendar year. It is an attribute of the course carried in the reference table, one row per AWARD_CODE, and is set by the accreditation decision rather than by anything the client did.
limitation: It is not the year the client earned anything. AWARD_DATE on amep_csweawards is the date of the client's assessment, and the two can be many years apart because an accredited course stays current for its whole accreditation period.
rationale: ASQA is the body named in the custodian's own wording, and its course accreditation page states what accreditation is and that ASQA grants it.
evidence_quote: ASQA accredits courses where a clearly demonstrated training need cannot be met through a nationally endorsed training package qualification.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the custodian's wording and the generic sentence twice over, so it never said that the year belongs to the course rather than the client, nor what an accredited course is.

value_domain: CSWE certificate level assigned at entry assessment
value_source: Department of Home Affairs, Evaluation of the Adult Migrant English Program New Business Model (Social Compass, 2019)
variable_description: The Certificates in Spoken and Written English level a client was placed at when they were first assessed, held once on the client profile. CSWE runs Preliminary, Certificate I, Certificate II and Certificate III, and the evaluation notes that Certificate III is "the highest level obtainable in the AMEP". The value is a placement judgement made at the start of tuition, so it is the closest thing the file has to a baseline English level under the pre-2017 curriculum.
value_definition: A CSWE certificate level. The four levels carry very different expected workloads: 210 to 660 supervised hours for Preliminary and 370 to 630 for Certificate III, with 1,415 to 2,430 supervised hours to move from beginner to Certificate III.
limitation: An entry level is not an award. The client has been placed at that level, not certified at it, and amep_csweawards is the only place a granted certificate appears. Entry assessment also moved to the Australian Core Skills Framework for new clients from 1 July 2017, so this column thins out for later cohorts rather than recording a genuine absence of assessment.
rationale: The evaluation sets out the CSWE level structure, the hours each level is expected to take, and the shift of initial assessment to the ACSF under the new business model, which is exactly what an entry level means and when it stops being recorded.
evidence_quote: Progress from total beginner to completion of Certificate III (the highest level obtainable in the AMEP) is expected to take between 1415 and 2430 supervised hours.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'CSWE level attained in entry assessment' with no value domain and the same generic sentence in both the definition and the limitation, so it neither listed the levels nor warned that a placement is not an attainment.

value_domain: Certificate level of the CSWE course
value_source: Department of Home Affairs, Evaluation of the Adult Migrant English Program New Business Model (Social Compass, 2019)
variable_description: The certificate level of a CSWE course, held once per award code on the AMEP award reference table. CSWE was the curriculum taught across the whole AMEP under the contract before July 2017, and its levels are Preliminary, Certificate I, Certificate II and Certificate III. The column describes the course, so it becomes a statement about a person only after joining AWARD_CODE to amep_csweawards.
value_definition: A CSWE certificate level attached to a course code. The reference table also carries the award name, description and accreditation year for the same code, so the level is one attribute of a course record rather than a client outcome.
limitation: The level is not scaled to the AMEP entitlement, and reading it as an achievable target misleads. Every level except Preliminary expects more than the 510 funded hours: Certificate I alone is 400 to 540 supervised hours and Certificate III is 1,070 to 1,330 total hours.
rationale: The evaluation gives the CSWE level structure and the hours each level requires, which is what distinguishes the levels and explains why few clients reach the higher ones inside their entitlement.
evidence_quote: For any level except preliminary, the lower limit of expected hours required to gain a certificate is more than 510.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed 'Certificate level of CSWE award/course' with the generic sentence duplicated, so it did not name the levels or say that the column belongs to a course reference table rather than to a client.

value_domain: AMEP tuition stream at the reporting date
value_source: Department of Home Affairs, Evaluation of the Adult Migrant English Program New Business Model (Social Compass, 2019)
variable_description: The tuition stream the client was in at the reporting date used for this extract, which for this file is a date before 1 July 2019. Streaming began with the new business model on 1 July 2017 and has two values. The evaluation says "Pre-Employment English is for those students who wish to participate in the workplace or further training and is mandatory for those referred to the AMEP by an employment services provider", while Social English is for clients improving conversational English to live independently in their community. INITIAL_STREAM holds the stream first assigned, so the pair shows whether a client moved.
value_definition: A two-category stream classification introduced under the 2017 AMEP contract. Pre-Employment English must use a nationally accredited curriculum; Social English may use non-accredited material and has larger classes and lighter teacher qualification requirements.
limitation: A blank is not a data fault for anyone whose AMEP participation ended before 1 July 2017, because streams did not exist then. The split is also far from even: the evaluation reports 77 per cent of classes as Pre-Employment English, 5 per cent as Social English and 18 per cent blended. Centrelink mutual obligation requirements do force some clients into Pre-Employment English, but the evaluation finds only five per cent of students are in that position, so the imbalance is not explained by that referral pathway.
rationale: The evaluation has a section on Targeted Tuition Streams that names the two streams, dates their introduction to July 2017 and explains their curriculum and enrolment differences.
evidence_quote: The two streams, Pre-Employment English and Social English, reflect the government's recognition that many students are seeking sustainable employment and would benefit from a stronger employment focus in their AMEP classes, while others are prioritising settlement in Australia and social participation within their community.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated 'Stream type at time of this reporting - prior to 01/07/19' with no value domain and one generic sentence used twice, so it never named the streams or said when streaming started.

value_domain: Date the AMEP file was extracted
value_source: ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA)
variable_description: The day Home Affairs pulled this AMEP table for delivery to the ABS, so it dates the snapshot rather than anything the client did. It is constant across the rows of a table and is the reason the hours panel stops where it does. Because each AMEP table was extracted on its own schedule, the value can differ between the hours, address, profile and assessment tables for the same person.
value_definition: A calendar date. The domain is open: any date on which the department produced the extract, which for the AMEP tables in PLIDA sits after the last quarter the hours columns cover.
limitation: It cannot be used as an end date for a client's participation. A client still enrolled on the extract date has an open, not a completed, history, and treating the extract date as an exit produces spuriously short spells.
rationale: The ABS page describes PLIDA as an asset built from agency extracts, which is the process this column dates; no published document gives the extract dates of the individual AMEP tables.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave 'Date data was extracted' and printed the generic sentence as both the definition and the limitation, so it did not distinguish file vintage from client history.

value_domain: Date of referral to a Distance Learning provider
value_source: Department of Home Affairs, Evaluation of the Adult Migrant English Program New Business Model (Social Compass, 2019)
variable_description: The date the client was referred to an AMEP Distance Learning provider, held once on the client profile. Distance Learning gives clients one-on-one classes with an AMEP teacher by phone or online rather than in a classroom, and every AMEP client is eligible for it even while attending face-to-face classes. In five remote contract regions there is no local provider at all, so a referral there reflects geography rather than a client's choice of mode.
value_definition: A calendar date. It is open ended and takes any date within the client's AMEP participation; there is no code list and no companion end date on the same row.
limitation: A referral is not a commencement or a volume of study. The AMEPDL and SPPDL quarterly hour columns are what show whether distance tuition actually happened, and childcare is not available for Distance Learning, so a referral here explains an empty CHILDCARE column rather than contradicting it.
rationale: The evaluation describes Distance Learning as one of the three AMEP delivery modes, its eligibility, and the remote regions that depend on it entirely.
evidence_quote: Distance Learning (DL): curriculum materials are mailed out to clients and discussed weekly, usually online in one-on-one sessions with a teacher.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed only 'Date when referred to Distance Learning provider' with the generic sentence twice over, so it did not say what Distance Learning is or how a referral relates to the DL hour columns.

value_domain: Self-reported employment status at AMEP registration
value_source: Department of Home Affairs, Evaluation of the Adult Migrant English Program New Business Model (Social Compass, 2019)
variable_description: The employment status the client stated about themselves when they registered with an AMEP provider, captured once and never updated. Registration is an early event: an eligible migrant must register within six months of arrival, so the answer describes someone who has usually been in Australia only weeks or months. It sits alongside the other self-reported registration fields, OCCUPATION_AT_REGISTRATION, HIGHEST_QUAL_AT_REGISTRATION and YEARS_OF_SCHOOLING.
value_definition: A short status code or label supplied by the client. The custodian publishes no code list for it and the field is not coded to the ABS labour force status classification, so the categories have to be read off the data.
limitation: It is not a labour force measure and will not agree with employment observed in tax or payroll data for the same person. The status is self-declared, in most cases by someone with less than functional English, and it is frozen at registration, so it cannot show a move into work during the program.
rationale: The evaluation establishes the registration timeframes and the eligibility test that fix when this answer is given and who gives it; no published source lists the response categories.
evidence_quote: They must register with an AMEP service provider within six months of their arrival in Australia (or within 12 months if they are under 18 years old), commence tuition within 12 months and finish within 5 years.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's wording with no value domain and one generic sentence used twice, so it did not flag that the value is self-reported, unclassified and fixed at a point very early in settlement.

value_domain: Australian financial year of first AMEP enrolment
value_source: Department of Home Affairs, Evaluation of the Adult Migrant English Program New Business Model (Social Compass, 2019)
variable_description: The Australian financial year in which the client first enrolled in, meaning first attended, the AMEP. Enrolment is a later step than registration: eligible clients "must register with an AMEP service provider within six months of their arrival in Australia ... commence tuition within 12 months and finish within 5 years", so this year can fall a year after arrival. It is the natural cohort variable for the file, because AMEP commencements, expenditure and retention are all reported by financial year.
value_definition: An Australian financial year running 1 July to 30 June, written as a year or year pair. It is derived from INITIAL_ENROLMENT_DATE on the same row rather than being reported separately.
limitation: It is not a year of arrival and not a calendar year. A May 2017 starter and an August 2017 starter sit in different cohorts three months apart, while that August 2017 starter shares a cohort with someone who began in June 2018; INITIAL_ARRIVAL_DATE is the field to use for time since migration.
rationale: The evaluation sets out the legislated registration, commencement and completion timeframes that separate arrival, registration and enrolment, and reports AMEP activity on a financial year basis throughout.
evidence_quote: They must register with an AMEP service provider within six months of their arrival in Australia (or within 12 months if they are under 18 years old), commence tuition within 12 months and finish within 5 years.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the custodian's wording, inferred a financial year domain from the name, and printed the generic sentence twice, so it never separated arrival from registration from first attendance.

value_domain: Indicator that the initial enrolment date was set by the overrides process
value_source: Department of Home Affairs, Evaluation of the Adult Migrant English Program New Business Model (Social Compass, 2019)
variable_description: A flag saying that INITIAL_ENROLMENT_DATE on this row was set through the overrides process rather than by normal provider reporting. Enrolment dates matter administratively because the legislated timeframes and the 510-hour entitlement clock hang off them. It is one of three override flags on the client profile, beside REGISTRATION_DATE_OVERRIDE and ENTITLEMENT_DATE_OVERRIDE.
value_definition: A two-state indicator, set or not set. It describes how the neighbouring date was arrived at, not what the date is, and no code list for the flag is published.
limitation: It does not record the original date, the reason for the change or who made it, so it cannot support any analysis of why enrolment dates move. Nor is it a general data-quality flag: an unset value says nothing about whether the enrolment date is right.
rationale: The evaluation documents that provider reporting into ARMS was cumbersome and that attendance and entitlement records were adjusted outside the system, which is the administrative context an override flag belongs to; the overrides process itself is not separately published.
evidence_quote: As ARMS only records full session attendance and approved absences, late arrivals, early departures and unapproved absences are accounted for on a spreadsheet and submitted through the ARF.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording, guessed a yes/no domain from the name, and printed one generic sentence in both the definition and the limitation, so it never said what the flag does and does not tell a reader.

value_domain: Indicator that the entitlement end date was set by the overrides process
value_source: Department of Home Affairs, Evaluation of the Adult Migrant English Program New Business Model (Social Compass, 2019)
variable_description: A flag saying that ENTITLEMENT_END_DATE on this row was set or changed through the department's overrides process. The entitlement end date is the deadline by which the client must finish their AMEP tuition, so moving it changes how long they have, not how many hours they hold. Read the two columns together: the flag is the only signal that the deadline on the row is an administrative decision rather than the standard calculation.
value_definition: A two-state indicator, set or not set. It qualifies the entitlement end date on the same row and has no published code list of its own.
limitation: An override does not mean extra hours. The 510-hour entitlement is separate from the deadline, and AMEP Extend, not an entitlement date override, is what adds tuition hours, so this flag cannot be used to find clients who received more tuition.
rationale: The evaluation sets out the legislated completion timeframe and the separate 510-hour entitlement, which is what distinguishes moving a deadline from granting more hours; the overrides process itself is not published.
evidence_quote: Since January 1993, Adult Migrant English Program (AMEP) students have had a legislated entitlement to 510 hours of language tuition.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed 'Whether ENTITLEMENT END DATE has been overrided through overrides process' with the generic sentence used twice, so it did not distinguish the deadline from the hours entitlement.

value_domain: Date the client's AMEP entitlement ends
value_source: Department of Home Affairs, Evaluation of the Adult Migrant English Program New Business Model (Social Compass, 2019)
variable_description: The date by which the client must have finished their AMEP tuition: a legislated deadline, not the day their hours run out. Eligible clients "must register with an AMEP service provider within six months of their arrival in Australia (or within 12 months if they are under 18 years old), commence tuition within 12 months and finish within 5 years". The date can be moved administratively, which ENTITLEMENT_DATE_OVERRIDE on the same row records.
value_definition: A calendar date, normally five years after the client's qualifying arrival or visa event. It is a legislated deadline rather than a code, and it is fixed on the client profile rather than recalculated as hours are used.
limitation: It is not a measure of entitlement remaining. A client can exhaust the 510 hours years before this date, and hours can be forfeited without the date moving: a quarter of students lost an average of 19 hours for unapproved absences, with 1,345 students forfeiting 50 hours or more.
rationale: The evaluation states the legislated registration, commencement and completion timeframes and separately explains the 510-hour entitlement and its forfeiture, which together fix what this date is and what it is not.
evidence_quote: They must register with an AMEP service provider within six months of their arrival in Australia (or within 12 months if they are under 18 years old), commence tuition within 12 months and finish within 5 years.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated 'Date when client's entitlement to AMEP ends' with the generic sentence in both the definition and the limitation, so a reader could not tell whether the field meant a deadline or an exhausted allocation.

value_domain: Lower bound of the first AMEP enrolment date range
value_source: Department of Home Affairs, Evaluation of the Adult Migrant English Program New Business Model (Social Compass, 2019)
variable_description: The earliest date of the range within which the client first enrolled in, meaning first attended, the AMEP. It is the opening half of a pair with FIRST_ENROLMENT_DATE_TO, and the pair appears on the hours and address tables in place of the exact date that the client profile table carries as INITIAL_ENROLMENT_DATE. Bounding rather than dating the event is what lets the wide hours panel be released without pinning a person to a day.
value_definition: A calendar date used as the lower bound of an interval. The interval is closed by FIRST_ENROLMENT_DATE_TO on the same row, and the two together describe one event, not a spell of enrolment.
limitation: It is not a start date for anything. Treating it as the day tuition began puts a client's first quarter of hours before their enrolment whenever the true date sits late in the range, and the range width is not published, so the size of that error cannot be bounded from the file.
rationale: The evaluation establishes what first enrolment means in the AMEP, that it is first attendance and that it follows registration; the paired from and to columns and their relationship to INITIAL_ENROLMENT_DATE are read from the registry itself rather than from a published document.
evidence_quote: They must register with an AMEP service provider within six months of their arrival in Australia (or within 12 months if they are under 18 years old), commence tuition within 12 months and finish within 5 years.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's wording and printed the generic sentence twice, so it did not say that the column is one end of a range or how it relates to INITIAL_ENROLMENT_DATE.

value_domain: Upper bound of the first AMEP enrolment date range
value_source: Department of Home Affairs, Evaluation of the Adult Migrant English Program New Business Model (Social Compass, 2019)
variable_description: The latest date of the range within which the client first enrolled in, meaning first attended, the AMEP. It closes the interval opened by FIRST_ENROLMENT_DATE_FROM, so the client's true first attendance sits somewhere between the two. Both columns repeat on every row of the hours and address tables, which is why they should be read as a bound on one event and not as a period of study.
value_definition: A calendar date used as the upper bound of an interval. It is always on or after FIRST_ENROLMENT_DATE_FROM on the same row, and the gap between them is an artefact of how the date was released rather than a fact about the client.
limitation: Subtracting the from date from this one does not give a duration of enrolment. It gives the width of the uncertainty around a single date, so using it as a spell length manufactures a programme participation that never happened.
rationale: The evaluation defines first enrolment as first attendance and places it after registration in the AMEP sequence; the paired bounding structure of these two columns is inferred from the registry.
evidence_quote: They must register with an AMEP service provider within six months of their arrival in Australia (or within 12 months if they are under 18 years old), commence tuition within 12 months and finish within 5 years.
supersedes_rationale: The entry duplicated the custodian's wording with the generic sentence in both the definition and the limitation, so nothing warned against reading the from and to pair as a start and an end of study.

value_domain: Mesh block (ASGS 2016) of the first AMEP training site
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS): Volume 1, July 2016, Mesh Blocks (MB)
variable_description: The mesh block containing the first site at which the client was taught, not where they live. Mesh blocks are "the smallest geographical area defined by the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS)", and the 2016 edition has 358,122 of them covering Australia without gaps or overlaps. The address table carries three other geographies for the same client, so this column has to be kept distinct from RESIDENTIAL_MB_ASGS_2016 and REGISTRATION_MB_ASGS_2016.
value_definition: An 11-digit ABS mesh block code on the July 2016 ASGS. Mesh blocks broadly identify land use, most populated ones hold 30 to 60 dwellings, and 113 of the 2016 codes are non-spatial special purpose codes for Migratory, Offshore, Shipping and No Usual Address.
limitation: It is a teaching location, so it will not behave like a residential geography. A training site often sits in a commercial or educational mesh block with no dwellings in it at all, which makes any dwelling-based or population-based measure computed on this column meaningless.
rationale: The ABS page for the July 2016 ASGS defines mesh blocks, gives their count, their design rules and the special purpose codes that appear in the domain.
evidence_quote: Mesh Blocks are the smallest geographical area defined by the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) and form the building blocks for the larger regions of the Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS).
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed 'First training site - Meshblock (ASGS 2016)' with the generic sentence twice, so it did not say what a mesh block is, which 2016 edition it belongs to, or that the geography describes a site rather than a person.

value_domain: Statistical Area Level 1 (ASGS 2016) of the first AMEP training site
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS): Volume 1, July 2016, Statistical Area Level 1 (SA1)
variable_description: The SA1 containing the first site at which the client was taught, which is the coarser companion to the mesh block on the same row. ABS SA1s are "geographical areas built from whole Mesh Blocks" and have "a population of between 200 and 800 people with an average population size of approximately 400 people", with 57,523 of them in the 2016 edition. It is the level most analysts will use, because SA1 is the smallest unit at which 2016 Census data was released.
value_definition: An SA1 code on the July 2016 ASGS: either the 11-digit fully hierarchical code or the truncated 7-digit code of state, SA2 and SA1 identifiers. SA1s aggregate whole mesh blocks and nest inside SA2, and 33 of the codes are non-spatial special purpose codes for Migratory, Offshore, Shipping and No Usual Address.
limitation: The site's SA1 is not a catchment and not the client's neighbourhood. Clients travel to class, so attaching SA1 Census characteristics to this column describes the area a provider chose to operate in, not the population it taught; LAST_TRAIN_SITE_SA1_ASGS_2016 differing on the same row shows how mobile the site itself can be.
rationale: The ABS page for the July 2016 ASGS defines SA1s, their construction from mesh blocks, their population range and their role as the smallest census release unit.
evidence_quote: Statistical Areas Level 1 (SA1) are geographical areas built from whole Mesh Blocks.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave 'First training site - SA1 (ASGS 2016)' and printed the generic sentence in both the definition and the limitation, so it neither described the SA1 unit nor warned that the geography belongs to a training site.

value_domain: Home Tutor Scheme hours attended, July to September 2011
value_source: Australian National Audit Office, performance audit 'Administration of the Adult Migrant English Program Contracts'
variable_description: Hours of Home Tutor Scheme tuition the client attended in the July to September quarter of 2011, the column named HTS_2011_Q3. HTS is the AMEP's volunteer tutor sub-program, the one-to-one scheme the ANAO records as the Home Tutor Scheme and later the Volunteer Tutor Scheme, and this column holds one quarter of it. A person's whole history runs across the 32 HTS columns of amep_clientshours_2011_19, not down the rows. A July to September column opens the financial year, which is when contract and funding changes take effect. This is the opening year of the wide file: the earlier table amep_clientshours_2003_11 carries no HTS series at all, only AMEP, AMEPDL, SLPT, SPP and SPPDL in yearly columns, so quarterly Home Tutor Scheme hours start here, with the program then run by the Department of Immigration and Citizenship under the 2011 AMEP contracts.
value_definition: A count of hours attended in the one quarter named in the column, held as a number with the client on the row. There is no code list: a zero, a whole or part-hour total and an empty cell are all possible, and the 32 HTS columns together span 1 July 2011 to 30 June 2019.
limitation: An empty cell does not mean the client wanted no tutoring. A client not yet registered, already exited, or waiting for a tutor match all leave the same blank as one who was enrolled and attended nothing, and the column carries no enrolment flag to separate them.
rationale: The ANAO audit of the AMEP contracts names the Home Tutor Scheme as one of the services the general service providers were contracted to deliver, which is what the abbreviation HTS stands for, and dates the contract and departmental changes that bracket this quarter.
evidence_quote: The approach to the market outlined the services the AMEP general service providers were to provide English language tuition and assessment (across two streams and sub-programs), child care and the Home Tutor Scheme (later renamed the Volunteer Tutor Scheme).
supersedes_rationale: The page showed the custodian's line 'HTS - number of hours attended by client in 2011 Quarter 3' with the generic no-value-list sentence printed as both the value definition and the limitation, and never said what HTS stands for.

value_domain: Home Tutor Scheme hours attended, October to December 2011
value_source: Australian National Audit Office, performance audit 'Administration of the Adult Migrant English Program Contracts'
variable_description: Hours of Home Tutor Scheme tuition the client attended in the October to December quarter of 2011, the column named HTS_2011_Q4. The measure is hours attended under the volunteer one-to-one tutor scheme, run alongside classroom tuition. It is stored wide: the client is the row and the quarter is the column name, so a series is read across the table rather than down it. An October to December column runs up to the end-of-year break. This is the opening year of the wide file: the earlier table amep_clientshours_2003_11 carries no HTS series at all, only AMEP, AMEPDL, SLPT, SPP and SPPDL in yearly columns, so quarterly Home Tutor Scheme hours start here, with the program then run by the Department of Immigration and Citizenship under the 2011 AMEP contracts.
value_definition: A count of hours attended in the one quarter named in the column, held as a number with the client on the row. There is no code list: a zero, a whole or part-hour total and an empty cell are all possible, and the 32 HTS columns together span 1 July 2011 to 30 June 2019.
limitation: Hours with a volunteer are not hours of teaching. The tutor is not an AMEP teacher and the scheme is not assessed, so this column cannot support a claim about tuition quality or about progress on the ACSF or a CSWE certificate.
rationale: The ANAO audit of the AMEP contracts names the Home Tutor Scheme as one of the services the general service providers were contracted to deliver, which is what the abbreviation HTS stands for, and dates the contract and departmental changes that bracket this quarter.
evidence_quote: The approach to the market outlined the services the AMEP general service providers were to provide English language tuition and assessment (across two streams and sub-programs), child care and the Home Tutor Scheme (later renamed the Volunteer Tutor Scheme).
supersedes_rationale: The entry left HTS as an unexpanded abbreviation and repeated one generic sentence for both the value definition and the limitation, so a reader could not tell volunteer tutoring from classroom tuition.

value_domain: Home Tutor Scheme hours attended, January to March 2012
value_source: Australian National Audit Office, performance audit 'Administration of the Adult Migrant English Program Contracts'

value_domain: SA2 code, ASGS 2016
value_source: Australian Bureau of Statistics, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS): Volume 1 - Main Structure and Greater Capital City Statistical Areas, July 2016, Statistical Area Level 2 (SA2)
variable_description: The SA2 holding the site where this client first attended AMEP tuition, coded to the 2016 ASGS. The ABS defines these as "medium-sized general purpose areas built up from whole Statistical Areas Level 1" whose "purpose is to represent a community that interacts together socially and economically", which makes an SA2 roughly a suburb or a country town and its surrounds. amep_address_2003_19 carries four geographies for a client at this level: the first training site, the last training site, the registration site and the residential address.
value_definition: A 9-digit fully hierarchical ASGS 2016 code, made of the state or territory digit, the SA4, the SA3 and a 4-digit SA2 identifier, drawn from the 2,310 SA2s of the 2016 edition. Eighteen of those are non-spatial special purpose codes for Migratory-Offshore-Shipping and No Usual Address.
limitation: It locates a building, not a person. A client who travelled across the city to reach a provider is counted in the provider's SA2, so mapping this column concentrates AMEP students on training centres and empties the suburbs they came from; RESIDENTIAL_SA2_ASGS_2016 on the same row answers the where-they-lived question.
rationale: The ABS publishes the 2016 edition of the ASGS, which is the edition the column name declares, and defines the SA2 and its coding structure there.
evidence_quote: Statistical Areas Level 2 (SA2) are medium-sized general purpose areas built up from whole Statistical Areas Level 1. Their purpose is to represent a community that interacts together socially and economically.
supersedes_rationale: The page repeated the custodian's 'First training site - SA2 (ASGS 2016)' and printed one generic sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so it never said what an SA2 is or that the location belongs to the provider and not the client.

value_domain: SA4 code, ASGS 2016
value_source: Australian Bureau of Statistics, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS): Volume 1 - Main Structure and Greater Capital City Statistical Areas, July 2016, Statistical Area Level 4 (SA4)
variable_description: The SA4 holding the site where this client first attended AMEP tuition, coded to the 2016 ASGS. SA4s are "the largest sub-State regions in the Main Structure" and are "specifically designed for the output of ABS Labour Force Survey data", so this column places a first training site in a labour market rather than a neighbourhood. It is the coarse member of the first-training-site set, which also holds meshblock, SA1 and SA2 codes for the same address.
value_definition: A 3-digit hierarchical ASGS 2016 code: a one-digit state or territory identifier followed by a two-digit SA4 identifier that is unique within that state, from the 107 SA4s of the 2016 edition.
limitation: An SA4 cannot identify a provider. Most SA4s contain several AMEP sites, so matching values for the first and last training site do not show that a client stayed at one centre, and a change of provider within a city is invisible here while it shows at SA2 or meshblock.
rationale: The 2016 ASGS volume defines the SA4, gives the 3-digit coding structure and states the labour market purpose that decides how coarse the column is.
evidence_quote: The SA4 regions are the largest sub-State regions in the Main Structure of the Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS), and have been designed for the output of a variety of regional data, including data from the 2016 Census of Population and Housing.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only 'First training site - SA4 (ASGS 2016)' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice over, so it gave no code shape and no reason to prefer the SA2 column for anything local.

value_domain: State and territory code, ASGS 2016
value_source: Australian Bureau of Statistics, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS): Volume 1 - Main Structure and Greater Capital City Statistical Areas, July 2016, Australia (AUS) and State | Territory (S|T)
variable_description: The state or territory of the site where this client first attended AMEP tuition, on the one-digit ASGS 2016 code. The ninth code is not a state: the ABS puts "Jervis Bay Territory, and the Territories of Christmas Island, Cocos (Keeling) Islands and Norfolk Island ... as one spatial unit at the State and Territory level under the category of Other Territories". The column's own metadata has no description, only the name repeated, so the ASGS edition has to be read from the sibling geography columns.
value_definition: A single digit: 1 New South Wales, 2 Victoria, 3 Queensland, 4 South Australia, 5 Western Australia, 6 Tasmania, 7 Northern Territory, 8 Australian Capital Territory, 9 Other Territories.
limitation: It is not the client's state of residence and not a settlement destination. A client who registered in one state and first attended in another shows the second here while REGISTRATION_STATE_ASGS_2016 shows the first, and a state total built from this column counts provider locations rather than migrants.
rationale: The 2016 ASGS volume publishes the state and territory codes used across the ASGS and explains what code 9 covers, which is the only part of the list a reader is likely to get wrong.
evidence_quote: States and Territories are identified by unique one-digit codes within Australia.
supersedes_rationale: The metadata line for this column was the variable name itself, FIRST_TRAIN_SITE_STATE_ASGS_2016, and the value definition and the limitation were the same generic sentence, so the page said nothing at all.

value_domain: Client's recorded gender
value_source: Australian Bureau of Statistics, Standard for Sex, Gender, Variations of Sex Characteristics and Sexual Orientation Variables
variable_description: The client's gender as recorded in ARMS when they registered with the AMEP, held once on the client profile rather than per event. The ABS standard treats this as a distinct concept from sex: "Gender is a social and cultural concept. It is about social and cultural differences in identity, expression and experience as a man, woman or non-binary person." The AMEP collection long predates that standard, so the categories in the data are the program's own operational ones and no code list is published with the data item list.
value_definition: A short code or label for gender, one value per client, entered at registration by a provider rather than derived. The domain is not published, so the categories present have to be read off the data.
limitation: It cannot be lined up with an ABS gender variable without first checking the codes. A field of this age usually offers two categories and an unknown, so an apparently zero non-binary count is evidence about the registration form and not about the client population.
rationale: The ABS standard supplies the concept the column name uses and the distinction between sex and gender that a reader needs, but no published page documents the AMEP field's own categories, so the code list stays unsourced.
evidence_quote: Gender is a social and cultural concept. It is about social and cultural differences in identity, expression and experience as a man, woman or non-binary person.
supersedes_rationale: The page carried 'Client's gender' from the data item list and the same generic sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so it neither named the concept nor warned that the categories are undocumented.

value_domain: Referral source reported at registration
value_source: Department of Home Affairs, Adult Migrant English Program - About the program
variable_description: How the client says they came to hear about the AMEP, captured once at registration. It is an outreach field rather than an eligibility one: Home Affairs promotes the program through providers, settlement services, employment services and a flyer published in many languages, and this column records which of those routes the client named. It sits with REGISTRATION_CENTRE and REGISTRATION_DATE, so it describes the moment of registration and not the moment of first attendance.
value_definition: A coded referral source, one value per client, with no code list published in the PLIDA data item list or on the department's AMEP pages.
limitation: It cannot measure what caused a person to enrol. Several routes usually apply at once, the answer is what the client recalled and what the officer coded, and a client registering again after an earlier spell may name the provider they already knew rather than the source that first reached them.
rationale: The department's AMEP pages describe the promotion channels the field is recording, but publish no category list for it, so the domain is inferred from the field's role rather than sourced.
supersedes_rationale: The entry was the custodian's 'Where client heard about AMEP from' with one generic sentence used for both the value definition and the limitation, and gave no warning that the field is self-reported and single-valued.

value_domain: Self-reported highest qualification at registration
value_source: Australian Bureau of Statistics, Australian Standard Classification of Education (ASCED), 2001
variable_description: The highest qualification the client said they held when they registered with the AMEP, taken from self-report and not verified. It covers overseas study as well as Australian, which is the point of collecting it, because a client with a foreign degree and no English is a different teaching problem from one with little schooling. YEARS_OF_SCHOOLING and YEARS_OF_TERTIARY_STUDY on the same row hold the duration side of the same self-report, and OCCUPATION_PRE_MIGRATION the work side.
value_definition: A coded qualification level, one value per client. The ABS publishes ASCED as the national standard for classifying attainment by level and field, but the data item list does not say the AMEP field is coded to it.
limitation: It will not line up with Census or ASCED attainment data unless you build the mapping yourself, and it is frozen at registration, so a qualification completed in Australia after enrolment never appears and an upward move over a client's AMEP years is invisible.
rationale: ASCED is the classification a reader would try to compare this field against, and the ABS page sets out what ASCED is for; nothing published states the AMEP field's own categories.
evidence_quote: The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) has developed the Australian Standard Classification of Education (ASCED) for use in the collection, storage and dissemination of statistical and administrative data relating to educational activity undertaken in Australia.
supersedes_rationale: The page repeated 'Highest qualification at time of registration with AMEP (self reporting)' and printed one generic sentence twice, so it did not say the field is fixed at registration or that it is not ASCED coded.

value_domain: ARMS row identifier for a CSWE award or course
value_source: Australian National Audit Office, performance audit 'Administration of the Adult Migrant English Program Contracts'
variable_description: The internal key for one Certificate in Spoken and Written English award or course in the AMEP reference table, and nothing about a person. ARMS is the "AMEP Reporting Management System", the departmental record store the ANAO describes as the program's legacy system, and amep_csweawardsrefcodes is its lookup list of CSWE awards. Each row pairs this identifier with AWARD_CODE, AWARD_NAME, AWARD_DESCRIPTION, CSWE_LEVEL and CSWE_ACCREDITATION_YEAR, which makes the table the decoder for AWARD_CODE in amep_csweawards.
value_definition: A surrogate identifier that is unique within the reference table, with no meaning outside ARMS and no relation to the certificate's national course code.
limitation: It is not the join key. amep_csweawards carries AWARD_CODE and not this identifier, so a join on ID quietly returns nothing, and because a certificate re-accredited in a later year takes a new reference row, one qualification can appear several times under different identifiers.
rationale: The ANAO audit names ARMS in full and describes its role as the AMEP's record system, which is what the phrase 'ARMS ID' in the custodian's wording refers to; the table's own columns show that it is a reference list rather than a client record.
evidence_quote: Administration and ownership of the AMEP Reporting Management System (ARMS) remained with the Department of Immigration and Citizenship.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed 'ARMS ID for CSWE award/course' with the generic no-value-list sentence as both the definition and the limitation, leaving ARMS unexplained and inviting a reader to join on the wrong column.

value_domain: Date of first ACSF assessment
value_source: Department of Employment and Workplace Relations, Australian Core Skills Framework
variable_description: The day the client's first Australian Core Skills Framework assessment was done, recorded for clients new to the AMEP from 1 July 2017. The ACSF is the tool the department describes as providing "a common language for describing performance in five core skills that support effective participation in society: learning, reading, writing, oral communication and numeracy". It dates the INITIAL_ ACSF indicator columns on the same row, while LATEST_ACSF_ASSESSMENT_DATE marks the other end of the client's assessed progress.
value_definition: A calendar date, one value per client, present only where an ACSF assessment was recorded, so in practice from 1 July 2017 onwards.
limitation: A blank does not mean the client was never assessed. Clients already enrolled before 1 July 2017 were assessed on the ASLPR instead, so this column and INITIAL_ASLPR_DATE split the file by enrolment era rather than by whether an assessment happened, and the two scales do not convert into one another.
rationale: The department publishes what the ACSF is and what it measures, which is the fact the column name assumes, and the contract date in the custodian's own wording fixes when the field starts.
evidence_quote: The Australian Core Skills Framework (ACSF) is a tool which provides a common language for describing performance in five core skills that support effective participation in society: learning, reading, writing, oral communication and numeracy.
supersedes_rationale: The page carried the custodian's line about the 1 July 2017 contract and one generic sentence for both the value definition and the limitation, so it never said what the ACSF is or why the column is empty for earlier clients.

value_domain: ACSF level on learning indicator .01
value_source: Department of Employment and Workplace Relations, Australian Core Skills Framework (full framework, Table 3: ACSF Performance Indicators)
variable_description: The ACSF level the client reached at their first assessment on learning indicator .01. The framework describes .01 as "Active awareness of self as a learner, planning and management of learning". The suffix in the column name is the indicator number and not a level, because the ACSF has "11 Indicators; two each for Learning, Reading, Writing and Oral Communication and three for Numeracy". INITIAL_LEARNING_02 holds the other learning indicator, and the AMEP file carries no numeracy indicators, .09 to .11, because the program teaches English.
value_definition: An ACSF level: Pre Level 1, which the framework covers in a separate supplement that is not organised against Indicators, or a whole level on the framework's "five levels of performance ranging from 1 (low level performance) to 5 (high level performance)". The framework writes level and indicator together, so a client at level 1 on learning has achieved both 1.01 and 1.02.
limitation: A level on one indicator is not the client's ACSF level. The eight English indicators the file carries, .01 to .08, can sit at different levels for the same person, so reporting an 'ACSF level' from this column alone hides exactly the profile the assessment was built to show.
rationale: Table 3 of the framework lists all eleven indicators against their core skills and descriptions, which is what decodes the numeric suffix in the column name, and the framework states the level range and the level.indicator notation.
evidence_quote: There are 11 Indicators; two each for Learning, Reading, Writing and Oral Communication and three for Numeracy.
supersedes_rationale: The page repeated the custodian's 'Initial ACSF assessment - Learning .01' and used one generic sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so a reader could not tell whether .01 was a level, a score or an indicator number.

value_domain: ASLPR rating, listening
value_source: D. E. Ingram, 'The ASLPR: Its Origins and Current Developments', ERIC record ED402735
variable_description: The client's listening rating at their first ASLPR assessment, which for most clients is their entry assessment into the AMEP. The ASLPR, in its co-author's words, is "a scale that describes how second language proficiency develops on a scale from zero to native-like proficiency, providing performance descriptions in terms of practical tasks", and it rates each macroskill separately, this column being the receptive spoken macroskill. INITIAL_ASLPR_DATE dates it and LATEST_ASLPR_LISTEN holds the same rating at the client's most recent assessment.
value_definition: A point on the ASLPR scale, which runs from 0 (zero proficiency) to 5 (native-like) across twelve rated points including the minus and plus steps such as 1- and 1+. Each macroskill is stated separately, in the form S:1+, L:2, R:1, W:1+.
limitation: A listening rating is not a comprehension test score and does not convert to IELTS or the CEFR. Listening and speaking are usually judged in the same interview, so the two columns are not independent observations and should not be averaged as though they were.
rationale: The ERIC record for the scale's co-author gives the ASLPR's own definition and its zero to native-like range, and the scale's publisher sets out the twelve rated points and the per-macroskill reporting the four columns follow.
evidence_quote: The Australian Second Language Proficiency Ratings (ASLPR) is a scale that describes how second language proficiency develops on a scale from zero to native-like proficiency, providing performance descriptions in terms of practical tasks.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed 'Initial ASLPR assessment listening' with the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so it never expanded ASLPR or gave the reader the range the rating sits on.

value_domain: Date of first ASLPR assessment
value_source: ISLPR Language Services, 'Summary of ISLPR | Marking Criteria'
variable_description: The day the client's first ASLPR English assessment was done, which dates the four INITIAL_ASLPR ratings on the same row. The scale's publisher describes it as "a detailed scale that describes real-life language behaviour at 12 levels from zero to native-like proficiency", assessed in an interview rather than a written test. LATEST_ASLPR_DATE dates the matching LATEST_ ratings, so the two dates bound whatever progress the pair of assessments shows.
value_definition: A calendar date, one value per client, present only where an ASLPR assessment was recorded. The domain is open and predates the ACSF columns on the same table.
limitation: It does not date the start of tuition. An assessment can sit weeks before enrolment or after it, so the gap to INITIAL_ENROLMENT_DATE is an administrative interval rather than a waiting time, and a blank marks a client assessed under the later ACSF regime rather than an unassessed one.
rationale: The scale's publisher states the number of rated levels and that assessment is of observed real-life language behaviour, which is what this date records the occasion of.
evidence_quote: The acronym, ISLPR, refers to a detailed scale that describes real-life language behaviour at 12 levels from zero to native-like proficiency.
supersedes_rationale: The page said only 'Date of initial ASLPR assessment' and repeated one generic sentence for both the value definition and the limitation, so it did not warn that an empty cell means a different assessment regime.

value_domain: Date of first AMEP enrolment
value_source: Department of Home Affairs, Adult Migrant English Program - About the program
variable_description: The day the client first attended AMEP tuition, which the custodian treats as the enrolment date rather than the day they signed up. Home Affairs keeps the two apart and, for a client whose eligible visa started after 1 October 2020, puts a deadline on each: they must "register with an AMEP provider within 6 months" and "start your course within 12 months" of that visa start date, so REGISTRATION_DATE and this column mark the ends of that window. Clients in this file enrolled between 2003 and 2019, under the time limits the ANAO records as removed by the April 2021 reforms rather than under this current wording. ENROLMENT_DATE_OVERRIDE beside it flags a date set through the department's overrides process rather than from attendance.
value_definition: A calendar date, one value per client. The address and hours tables hold the same fact only as a banded pair, FIRST_ENROLMENT_DATE_FROM and FIRST_ENROLMENT_DATE_TO, rather than as an exact day.
limitation: It marks a first attendance, not a spell of study. A client who came once and never returned carries the same value as one who studied for years, and because the hours tables give only a date range, the exact day cannot be recovered when working from those tables alone.
rationale: The department's own program page distinguishes registering from starting a course and attaches separate deadlines to each, which is the distinction between REGISTRATION_DATE and this column.
evidence_quote: You have time limits for registering, starting and finishing the program from your eligible visa start date.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated 'Date when client first enrolled in (first attended) AMEP' with one generic sentence twice over, and did not tell a reader that the same fact is banded in the other AMEP tables.

value_domain: Date of first arrival in Australia
value_source: Department of Home Affairs, Adult Migrant English Program - About the program
variable_description: The day the client first arrived in Australia, carried onto the AMEP record from departmental visa information rather than reported by the client. It is settlement context and not an eligibility clock: Home Affairs states that "Your eligible visa start date decides the time you have to join and learn English with the AMEP", so INITIAL_VISA_GRANT_DATE and not this column drives the deadlines. The gap between arrival and INITIAL_ENROLMENT_DATE is the quantity worth building, because it measures how long a migrant waited before starting English tuition.
value_definition: A calendar date, one value per client, sourced from departmental records and grouped with the other visa fields on amep_cltpro_dob_visa_treated.
limitation: It is a first arrival, not the arrival that led to settlement. Someone who holidayed here years before migrating carries that earlier date, and an onshore applicant who changed visa in Australia has an arrival unconnected to the visa that made them eligible, so a years-since-arrival measure is wrong for both.
rationale: The department's program page makes the eligible visa start date, not arrival, the trigger for the AMEP time limits, which is the confusion this column invites; the field's own grouping under 'Visa information' shows where the date comes from.
evidence_quote: Your eligible visa start date decides the time you have to join and learn English with the AMEP.
supersedes_rationale: The page carried 'Visa information - Client's initial arrival date in Australia' and the same generic sentence as both definition and limitation, so it implied the arrival date sets AMEP entitlement when the visa start date does.

value_domain: Date the client's initial visa was granted
value_source: Department of Home Affairs, Adult Migrant English Program - About the program
variable_description: The day the client's first visa was granted, held on the AMEP record because the visa start date sets their program deadlines. Home Affairs splits clients on it: those whose eligible visa started on or before 1 October 2020 "can stay in the AMEP until you reach a vocational level of English" with no time limits, while later starters must register within six months, start within twelve and finish within five years. Read with VISA_SUBCLASS, VISA_MIGRATION_CATEGORY and LEGISLATIVE_ELIGIBILITY it says which eligibility regime a client falls under.
value_definition: A calendar date, one value per client, taken from departmental visa records rather than client report.
limitation: It is the first visa, not necessarily the AMEP-eligible one. A client who arrived on a student or visitor visa and later took a permanent visa carries the earlier grant date here, so using it as the eligible visa start date puts them under the wrong deadline rule and can make an on-time enrolment look late.
rationale: The department's program page ties the registration, commencement and completion limits to the eligible visa start date and gives 1 October 2020 as the dividing line, which is what makes this date the operative one on the client profile.
evidence_quote: You can stay in the AMEP until you reach a vocational level of English.

value_domain: SLPET tuition hours attended in the calendar year

variable_description: Hours of SLPET tuition the client attended during the 2009 calendar year. SLPT is the file's short name for the Settlement Language Pathways to Employment and Training subprogram; the Department of Home Affairs evaluation of the AMEP new business model records that before July 2017 the program offered "up to an additional 200 hours under the Settlement Language Pathways to Employment and Training (SLPET) subprogram". value_definition: A count of tuition hours held as a number, not a code, and zero or missing for a client with no SLPET activity in the year. This table alternates calendar-year and financial-year columns of the same measure, so consecutive columns are not consecutive periods.
limitation: An empty or zero year usually means there was no SLPET enrolment in that period at all, not an enrolment with no attendance, so the column measures whether the client took the vocational course as much as how hard they worked at it.
